tips.advancedSettings.text: After a coding agent's update, Hive no longer sees its trust question or its sign-in errors? Settings → Advanced has the text and fields Hive looks for, and its timeouts: change one, with the default beside it, or edit advanced.json.
tips.advancedSettings.title: Fix a CLI change yourself
tips.agentConsole.text: Settings → Agent API → Let agents read the developer console gives agents a read-only tool showing their CLI's hooks and status line next to what Hive made of each, redacted, so they can debug what Hive sees.
tips.agentConsole.title: Let agents see what their CLI sends
tips.agentLayouts.text: Each agent has its own pane: choose a layout at the right of the session toolbar, and drag a pane by its header to rearrange them. File locks stop two agents editing the same file.
tips.agentLayouts.title: Several agents side by side
tips.agentMenu.text: An agent's pane header keeps to its state, its card and Stop. Compact, Hand Over, Merge…, its settings and anything that needs a look (a dot on ⋯ says so) are in its ⋯ menu, or right-click the header. {key}
tips.agentMenu.title: Everything else is under an agent's ⋯
tips.agentSettings.text: Click an agent's model in its footer for Agent Settings: give a reviewer a faster model while another agent codes with the strongest.
tips.agentSettings.title: A model per agent
tips.agentStates.text: Each agent has one of four states, told apart by shape as well as colour: a diamond waits for you, a square is stalled, a pulsing dot is working and a ring is idle. The project header counts them: "1 waiting · 2 working".
tips.agentStates.title: Read your agents at a glance
tips.alwaysOnTop.text: The pin in the title bar (or Ctrl+Alt+O) keeps the window above your other apps, so a test run or an emulator can work underneath. Each window has its own, remembered for its workspace.
tips.alwaysOnTop.title: Keep a Hive window on top
tips.antivirus.text: On Windows, Microsoft Defender scans every file builds, tests and git touch. Settings → Workspace → Antivirus scanning shows whether it scans your workspace and can exclude its folders, with your consent.
tips.antivirus.title: Antivirus and your workspace
tips.archiveNew.text: The cheapest way to carry on after a long session: archive it and start clean, so nothing old is re-cached. Write a handover first so the new one knows where to pick up.
tips.archiveNew.title: Archive and Start New
tips.assistant.text: The panel on the right oversees the workspace: ask what the agents are doing, what things cost, or for a plan. {key}
tips.assistant.title: Ask the Hive Assistant
tips.assistantBatch.text: The Assistant can move or label up to {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} in one step, each card still listed on its own. The step counts as one of its {changes, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} for a message, so it never stops part-way through them.
tips.assistantBatch.title: Many cards in one step
tips.assistantCompact.text: The Assistant usually works with a bigger context than your agents, so its Compact button turns orange later: past {tokens, plural, one {# token} other {# tokens}} by default. Settings → Assistant → Highlight Compact over changes that, or Never turns it off.
tips.assistantCompact.title: When the Assistant suggests compacting
tips.assistantControl.text: Settings → Assistant → Control decides what it may do: only advise, or also add, start and brief agents and start cards when you ask.
tips.assistantControl.title: Let the Assistant run agents
tips.assistantImages.text: The Assistant view's Attachments shows every screenshot and file you've pasted or dropped into its conversations, by conversation. Click a conversation's name to read it again.
tips.assistantImages.title: What you've attached to the Assistant
tips.assistantJournal.text: The Assistant keeps a journal in each workspace: decisions, plans and what happened, recalled a few lines at a time after a restart. Settings → Assistant → Journal chooses what it may store, or turns it off.
tips.assistantJournal.title: The Assistant remembers
tips.assistantJournalBrowser.text: The Assistant view's Journal shows what the Assistant keeps in its journal, newest first. Search it, open an entry to correct or delete it, or use Forget These… to remove everything a search finds.
tips.assistantJournalBrowser.title: Read what the Assistant remembers
tips.assistantLaneWatch.text: Running several lanes, the Assistant waits on all of them at once and is woken only for a failed review, a blocked or stalled card, a lane ready to merge or one that ended.
tips.assistantLaneWatch.title: One watch for all the lanes
tips.assistantLanes.text: When the Assistant starts an agent on its next set of cards, it gives it a new conversation in the same step (the old one stays in the Sessions tab). Short conversations cost much less: ask it to do the same for any new card.
tips.assistantLanes.title: A new conversation for each lane
tips.assistantMessages.text: The Assistant can't give a waiting or working agent a new task, but it can leave it a message, such as your answer: delivered as soon as the agent can take it. Its pane shows it as unread (✉) until then; click that to cancel it.
tips.assistantMessages.title: The Assistant can reach a busy agent
tips.assistantReplies.text: When you answer an agent in its pane while the Assistant watches it or its card, the Assistant is told the first line, so it doesn't ask you again. Settings → General → Your name sets how it names you; Settings → Assistant turns it off.
tips.assistantReplies.title: The Assistant hears your answers to agents
tips.assistantSettings.text: Not sure which setting would help? Ask the Assistant: it explains any of them and says where it is. With Settings → Assistant → Control → Change settings on, it can make the change, which you can revert from its panel.
tips.assistantSettings.title: Ask the Assistant about a setting
tips.assistantSide.text: Windows notifications or another app covering the right of the screen? View → Move Assistant Panel to the Left puts the Assistant beside the project list.
tips.assistantSide.title: The Assistant on the left
tips.assistantStatus.text: The line under the Assistant's header says what it is doing, and which cards it waits on and until when: click one to open it. Done by the Assistant at its end lists what it did. Under Workspace, hover an agent's mark for what it's doing; click to go there.
tips.assistantStatus.title: What the Assistant is doing
tips.assistantTeam.text: With three or more agents, or builders and reviewers, ask the Assistant in Coordinator mode to run your cards as lanes: it splits them by the files they touch, briefs each pair and watches every lane to the end. With one or two agents it keeps out of the way.
tips.assistantTeam.title: The Assistant runs your team
tips.assistantToldWaiting.text: While the Assistant watches the lanes, an agent showing a permission prompt or asking you something wakes it, and it tells you which agent, its card and what it asks. It never answers for you. Its watch can follow a release card outside the lanes too.
tips.assistantToldWaiting.title: The Assistant tells you when an agent needs you
tips.assistantWaits.text: Ask the Assistant to let you know when an agent finishes a build or a test run: it waits without checking in, and Hive wakes it when the agent finishes, needs you or stops.
tips.assistantWaits.title: Have the Assistant tell you when an agent is done
tips.attachFiles.text: Drop a PDF, a log or any file onto an agent's terminal: Hive keeps a copy with the session and pastes its path. A chip shows what's attached, and says when the agent's CLI doesn't read that kind of file itself, so the agent opens it by its path.
tips.attachFiles.title: Attach any file to a prompt
tips.banners.text: While you use Hive, an agent finishing or needing you is a banner in the window, not a Windows notification over the Assistant. Settings → Notifications chooses where it shows, for which workspaces, and for how long.
tips.banners.title: Notices in Hive, not over it
tips.board.text: Cards in On Hold, Todo, Doing, Review, Passed and Done, each for a project. Start… gives a card to an agent with the card as its prompt. {key}
tips.board.title: Plan work on the task board
tips.boardArchive.text: Tick Archived on the board for a table of archived cards: sort and filter them by project, label or the column they came from, and Unarchive one or a whole selection.
tips.boardArchive.title: Find an archived card
tips.boardArchiveAll.text: A column's ⋯ has Archive All in Done (n)…, and the board's ⋯ has Archive All Cards… for every column. Cards agents are on are skipped unless you say, and Undo puts everything back where it was.
tips.boardArchiveAll.title: Clear a column in one go
tips.boardDoing.text: Drag a card into Doing and Hive asks: nobody yet, an agent without starting anything, or an agent that starts on it now.
tips.boardDoing.title: Choose who works on a card in Doing
tips.boardDone.text: A reviewer moves a card that passes its review to Passed; Done means merged, and an agent moves its cards there after merging its work. Say "merged, move #65 to done" and it does; the card's history shows who moved it.
tips.boardDone.title: Passed, then Done once merged
tips.boardExport.text: The board is kept in the workspace's database. Export Board to JSON… in the board's ⋯ menu saves every card as a JSON file, archived ones too, in a folder you choose.
tips.boardExport.title: Your board as plain files
tips.boardFold.text: Collapse a column to a narrow strip with the « in its header, and fold cards to one line with their ▾; a column's ⋯ collapses or expands all its cards. Hive remembers them for the workspace.
tips.boardFold.title: Fold the board to what matters
tips.boardOrder.text: Drag the most important cards to the top, or ask the Assistant or an agent to prioritise: they reorder the board itself.
tips.boardOrder.title: A column's order is its priority
tips.boardReview.text: Say "review #87" to another agent: the card stays in Review with the agent that did the work, shows who is reviewing it, and gets the verdict as a comment. When it passes, the reviewer moves it to Passed.
tips.boardReview.title: Have an agent review a card
tips.boardSetAside.text: Opened in an older Hive, a workspace gets its cards set aside when this one opens it again. Review… on the notice, or Set-Aside Cards… in the board's ⋯ menu, adds each to the board or discards it.
tips.boardSetAside.title: Cards made by an older Hive
tips.cardCost.text: A card's panel says what its agents used while they held it, "{example}", with the builder's and reviewer's parts and tokens on hover. Performance lists every card's cost, and a lane's hover in the Progress panel its overhead.
tips.cardCost.title: What a card cost
tips.cardDecisions.text: A card's Decisions, above its comments, hold what you decided: agents check their work against them before Review, and reviewers fail work that ignores one. Tell the Assistant a decision and it records it there; an agent waiting for your answer is told.
tips.cardDecisions.title: Put what you decide on the card
tips.cardLinks.text: Card numbers an agent or the Assistant prints, like #12, are links: hover one for its title and column, and Ctrl+click it to open the card.
tips.cardLinks.title: Ctrl+click a card number in the terminal
tips.cardLoop.text: Tell one agent to work through some cards as the builder and another to review them: each waits for the other at no cost, and Hive wakes it when the card changes.
tips.cardLoop.title: Let two agents build and review in turn
tips.cardMove.text: Drag any dialog by its header (a card, Add Agent, Agent Settings…) to see what's behind it; Escape while dragging puts it back.
tips.cardMove.title: Move a dialog out of the way
tips.cardSummaries.text: Agents start a card's report or review verdict with one line saying what is ready or what was found, the details below; they and the Assistant read just those lines when that's enough.
tips.cardSummaries.title: Reports start with the gist
tips.closeWindow.text: With several windows open, File → Close Window ({key}) closes just this one, as its X does. Exit Hive (all windows) closes every window and stops all their agents.
tips.closeWindow.title: Close one window, or all of them
tips.compactFocus.text: Compact summarises the conversation so every later message costs less. Give it a focus ("keep the API decisions, drop the test output") and the agent keeps what matters. {key}
tips.compactFocus.title: Compact with a focus
tips.compactSidebar.text: Toggle Compact Sidebar turns the project list into a narrow rail of tiles with each project's agents, leaving more room for the terminals.
tips.compactSidebar.title: A compact project list
tips.compactionHistory.text: The Overview's compaction history pages, filters and sorts a long session's compactions; click one to read it in the transcript, with the summary the agent carried on from.
tips.compactionHistory.title: Read a compaction where it happened
tips.consoleRecording.text: In the developer console, Record writes what an agent's CLI sends Hive to a file, redacted unless you tick text for that recording, and Copy Diagnostics can attach it to a bug report.
tips.consoleRecording.title: Record what a CLI sends
tips.consoleText.text: Settings → Advanced → Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text shows them in the developer console, under a banner saying so, and ticks text for new recordings. Tokens and sign-ins stay masked, and agents' hive_console stays redacted.
tips.consoleText.title: See the text in the developer console
tips.copilot.text: Agents can use the GitHub Copilot CLI, Copilot Free included. Agent Setup installs it and says who it is signed in as: its own login or the GitHub CLI’s.
tips.copilot.title: Run agents on GitHub Copilot
tips.copilotModes.text: Copilot agents start in Accept edits: they edit files in their own folder and use the hive tools without asking, and ask before other commands, other MCP tools and web access. Choose Ask to approve each edit too, or Allow all to approve everything.
tips.copilotModes.title: What Copilot agents ask before
tips.copyDiagnostics.text: Help → Copy Diagnostics… gathers Hive's version, your coding agents, key settings and the end of the log for a bug report, with names, folders and tokens taken out.
tips.copyDiagnostics.title: Found a bug? Copy Diagnostics
tips.dateFormat.text: Hive shows dates as {date} and times as {time}. Settings → General → Date format and Time format change them everywhere, sessions named by when they started too.
tips.dateFormat.title: Dates your way
tips.defaultProvider.text: Default provider is Automatic unless you choose one: new agents use the first coding agent that is turned on and installed, so Codex or GitHub Copilot alone works without Claude Code. Choose one in Settings → Providers to always use it.
tips.defaultProvider.title: New agents use what you have installed
tips.developerConsole.text: Turn on Settings → Advanced → Show developer features, then Help → Developer Console opens a window of its own: pick an agent and see each hook and status line beside what Hive made of it, redacted. Filter, search and pause as it runs.
tips.developerConsole.title: Watch what a CLI sends Hive
tips.editTemplates.text: Select a template in the Templates view and choose Edit…: add, copy, reorder or remove its agents, change each in the Agent Settings dialog (its Save saves the template too), rename it and pick its layout.
tips.editTemplates.title: Edit a template in place
tips.fileLinks.text: File paths an agent prints, like src/app.ts:42, are links: Ctrl+click one to open the file in the Files tab at that line.
tips.fileLinks.title: Ctrl+click a path in the terminal
tips.filesTab.text: The Files tab browses and edits the project, previews Markdown, CSV, HTML and images, and keeps unsaved edits as you switch.
tips.filesTab.title: Edit files without leaving Hive
tips.gitCheck.text: Help → Agent Setup… shows the git Hive found and its version. Worktree agents, merging and the Git tab need Git for Windows 2.38 or later.
tips.gitCheck.title: Is git ready for worktrees?
tips.gitInit.text: A project without git? Its Git tab's Initialise repository… makes it one on main, keeps .hive out, adds a starter .gitignore if you like and makes the first commit, so agents can work in worktrees at once.
tips.gitInit.title: Make a project a git repository in one click
tips.gitView.text: The Git tab shows its branch, remotes, history and tags, and lets you switch or create a branch, fetch, pull, push, tag and set its commit identity. The status bar shows "{example}": click it to get there.
tips.gitView.title: See and change a project's git
tips.gotoProject.text: Press {key} and type a few letters of its name.
tips.gotoProject.title: Jump to a project
tips.handoverSelf.text: When an agent's transcript size turns amber, click it and choose the agent itself: it writes a handover, and a new conversation picks up from it, short and fast again.
tips.handoverSelf.title: A long conversation? Hand it over to itself
tips.hardwareAcceleration.text: If your graphics driver leaves Hive's window blank, flickering or crashing, turn on Settings → Advanced → Disable hardware acceleration and restart Hive. A window that doesn't draw at all: start Hive once with --disable-gpu.
tips.hardwareAcceleration.title: A blank or flickering window?
tips.hiveFolder.text: Hive keeps each project's .hive folder (sessions, backups, launch settings) out of git by itself. Where it can't, say with no git, another version control system, or a folder OneDrive or Dropbox syncs, the project's Overview tells you.
tips.hiveFolder.title: A project's .hive stays on this computer
tips.hiveSkills.text: Agents and the Assistant get Hive's own skills: work-on-card, review-agent-work, handover and more. Hive keeps them up to date; ones you edit stay yours.
tips.hiveSkills.title: Skills for working with Hive
tips.imagesTab.text: The Attachments tab keeps each screenshot and file pasted or dropped into the project's sessions, grouped by session, with previews and a filter by kind, ready to insert again.
tips.imagesTab.title: Everything you attached, in one place
tips.improveTranslation.text: Spotted a clumsy or wrong word in your language? Help → Improve This Translation shows how to fix it, or add a language, with a pull request on GitHub.
tips.improveTranslation.title: Make Hive read better in your language
tips.inboxNotices.text: A message the Assistant leaves a working agent reaches it at its next tool call, or before its turn ends, as a short notice from Hive: nothing is typed over its work. The agent reads it from its inbox and acks it; its pane shows it as unread (✉) until it does.
tips.inboxNotices.title: Messages reach a busy agent between steps
tips.keepAwake.text: While an agent works, Hive stops Windows from sleeping (the screen can still lock), and lets it sleep once they're done. Choose when in Settings → General.
tips.keepAwake.title: Leave agents working, the PC stays awake
tips.language.text: Hive follows Windows' display language when it has it. Settings → General → Language picks another; languages translated by AI are marked, and improvements are welcome. Agents are still spoken to in English.
tips.language.title: Hive in your language
tips.leftoverProcesses.text: A preview server or a tail -f an agent started can keep running after it stops, holding the project's folder or a port. Hive lists them in the ⋯ menu on the agent's pane and offers to end them; Settings → Agents can end them every time.
tips.leftoverProcesses.title: End what a stopped agent left running
tips.loopDefaults.text: Settings → Workspace → Card loop rounds and Card loop wait set what loops use when you don't say ({rounds, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}} and {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} to start with); a project can have its own. Saying "rounds: 3" when you start one still wins.
tips.loopDefaults.title: Your rounds and wait for every loop
tips.loopLanes.text: When two agents build and review cards in turn, Hive keeps the loop as a lane: its cards in order, the one it's on, and whether it's paused on a blocked card. Ask the Assistant which lanes are running.
tips.loopLanes.title: Hive keeps your card loops as lanes
tips.loopWakes.text: When a card arrives in Review, Hive wakes its reviewer, and on the verdict its builder, even if one forgot to wait. To drive reviews by hand, turn it off in the project's Settings → Card loops.
tips.loopWakes.title: Loops keep going on their own
tips.mcpFromFile.text: Got a server as a .json definition or a .zip of its folder? Add MCP Server from File in the MCP view shows what it runs and adds it turned off: switch it on there to choose its projects.
tips.mcpFromFile.title: Add an MCP server from a file
tips.mcpPerAgent.text: In an agent's settings, MCP servers: Only these gives it just the servers it needs, such as a sandbox server for a release tester, and keeps the others' tools out of its context.
tips.mcpPerAgent.title: MCP servers for some agents only
tips.mcpPerProject.text: A workspace MCP server runs in a project only when it's on in the workspace (its switch in the MCP view, which asks for the projects) and on in that project's MCP tab. Its tools stay out of the other projects' agents' context.
tips.mcpPerProject.title: MCP servers only where they are needed
tips.memorySnapshot.text: Turn on Settings → Advanced → Save a memory snapshot if Hive is about to run out of memory, to find out what filled it. Snapshots can be gigabytes, hold what Hive had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stay on this PC.
tips.memorySnapshot.title: Hive closed running out of memory?
tips.mergeSlot.text: When several agents finish at once, each claims the project's merge slot before it merges main in, checks and merges, so nobody's checks have to run twice. Who holds it and who waits shows in the Overview and the Progress panel.
tips.mergeSlot.title: Agents take turns to merge
tips.messageReceipts.text: Every message the Assistant leaves an agent has an id and is kept, even across a restart: it is received once the agent reads its inbox, and acked once the agent acted on it. One not acked within {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} shows as overdue (✉) in its pane.
tips.messageReceipts.title: See where a message got to
tips.modelFallbacks.text: Hive asks Claude Code and Codex which models they have and which effort levels each takes. If a CLI can't say, the model, effort and price lists on its Settings page are yours to edit.
tips.modelFallbacks.title: New models without a Hive update
tips.moreAgents.text: Need more than {usual, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}} in a project? Raise Agents per project in Settings → Advanced, up to {most, number}, for every workspace or just this one. Above {usual, number} it shows what they cost on your computer: the memory your running agents take, and how much is free.
tips.moreAgents.title: More than {usual, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}}
tips.myPrices.text: Claude Code's cost is its own figure, from its price table. On other rates (a discount, another tier)? Set Session costs to My prices, and Hive prices every session from your table instead.
tips.myPrices.title: Your own prices for Claude Code
tips.newCard.text: Press {key} for a new card for the project you are in, without leaving what you are doing.
tips.newCard.title: Jot down a card
tips.off.message: Help → Tips… still has them, and Settings → General turns them back on.
tips.off.title: Tips are off
tips.overview.text: The Workspace Overview shows what every project used, what runs now and the board, by day. {key}
tips.overview.title: The whole workspace at a glance
tips.ownShortcuts.text: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts changes any shortcut, and Project Settings can change them for one project.
tips.ownShortcuts.title: Make the shortcuts yours
tips.palette.text: Press {key} and type: every command, with its shortcut.
tips.palette.title: Everything is in the command palette
tips.pasteScreenshot.text: Press Ctrl+V in an agent's terminal with an image on the clipboard, or drop an image onto it: the agent sees it, and Hive keeps a copy.
tips.pasteScreenshot.title: Paste a screenshot into a session
tips.perfCompare.text: Performance → Compare: keep the current view before a change and again after it, and see whether Hive’s traffic fell while the work still got done.
tips.perfCompare.title: Before and after a change
tips.performance.text: Performance, in the activity bar, shows what Hive's API, tools and guidance cost for the last day, week or month: the whole workspace or one project. Each project has its own Performance tab too.
tips.performance.title: What Hive itself costs
tips.permissionMode.text: Click the mode in an agent's footer, or press {key}, to move between asking first, accepting edits and planning.
tips.permissionMode.title: Switch permission mode
tips.personas.text: Coordinator runs the agents, Planner shapes work, QA triager turns reports into cards, Release manager takes a release through its checklist. Switch mode from the panel at once, keeping the conversation, or write your own.
tips.personas.title: Modes for the Assistant
tips.progressCommand.text: Agents run long commands such as tests and builds through hive-progress, so the Progress panel shows them under the agent's name, with about how long is left from the second time. Settings can have them do it only when you ask.
tips.progressCommand.title: Progress for any command
tips.progressDetails.text: Click a run in the Progress panel, or one under Recent, for its details: the whole command, when it ran and how long it took, its exit code, the log it wrote and why it failed.
tips.progressDetails.title: What did that run do?
tips.progressFilter.text: When several projects run tests and builds, the dropdown at the top of the Progress panel shows just one project's runs, or one agent's. Each workspace remembers the choice.
tips.progressFilter.title: Only one project's runs
tips.progressHistory.text: Recent in the Progress panel shows the last {recent, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}}; Show all scrolls through the last {kept, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}}, even after Hive restarts. The project filter applies to them all.
tips.progressHistory.title: What ran this morning?
tips.progressLanes.text: When pairs of agents work through cards, the bottom of the Progress panel shows each lane as a bar, a segment per card coloured by where it is. Hover one for its card and round; click to open it. A merge going on shows as a teal card at the top.
tips.progressLanes.title: How far along is each pair?
tips.progressLanesHeight.text: The Progress panel shows up to four lanes. Drag the line above Lanes up to see more, a whole lane at a time; double-click it to go back to four. Each workspace remembers it.
tips.progressLanesHeight.title: See more lanes at once
tips.progressLanesOrder.text: Drag a running lane up or down in the Progress panel, or focus it and press Alt+Up or Alt+Down. Each workspace keeps your order; a new lane comes in on top, and merged ones drop to the bottom.
tips.progressLanesOrder.title: Put your lanes in order
tips.progressPanel.text: When agents run tests or builds that report progress, the Progress panel on the right shows each run: the agent, how far along it is and the time left, and Hive's taskbar button fills as they go. {key} shows it.
tips.progressPanel.title: How long until the tests finish?
tips.projectCards.text: A project's Overview starts with its cards: how many are in each column, stalled or blocked. Click a number to open its Tasks tab.
tips.projectCards.title: A project's cards at a glance
tips.projectTabs.text: When space is short, a project's tabs shrink to icons, and the tab you're on keeps its name while it fits. Hover a tab for its name and shortcut.
tips.projectTabs.title: Tabs that make room
tips.projectTabsKeys.text: Alt+1 to Alt+8 open a project's tabs in the order they show, Session to Git. Memory, Skills, Templates and MCP are in More ▾ at the end, and in the menu bar's Project menu.
tips.projectTabsKeys.title: Alt and a number for each tab
tips.quitWhenDone.text: Quitting while an agent works offers Quit when agents finish: Hive hides and quits by itself once they're done. Conversations are always kept.
tips.quitWhenDone.title: Quit when agents finish
tips.recentWorkspaces.text: Remove a workspace from File → Open Recent or the welcome page with its ✕, or right-click it. Clear Recently Opened forgets them all; folders that are gone show as not found.
tips.recentWorkspaces.title: Tidy your recent workspaces
tips.removeAll.text: Remove All in the project header removes all of a project's agents after one question. Worktrees are kept unless you tick the box, which deletes only merged, clean ones.
tips.removeAll.title: Remove every agent at once
tips.resumeAll.text: After a restart, Resume All Agents in the project header resumes every stopped agent's last session in one go.
tips.resumeAll.title: Resume all agents at once
tips.safeguardStops.text: A shield beside an agent's status means its CLI's safety classifier stopped a response: hover it for when, the model, and the agent's last tool calls before it. Orange means its model changed since, or it waits on you.
tips.safeguardStops.title: See when a safety classifier stops an agent
tips.saveTemplate.text: Set agents up once and reuse them: + Add ▾ → Templates → Save Template… in the session toolbar keeps their settings, roles and layout, and the same menu loads them into any project.
tips.saveTemplate.title: Save your agents as a template
tips.searchClear.text: Every search and filter box has an × while it has text: click it, or press Escape, to see everything again. In a dialog or the palette, the next Escape closes it.
tips.searchClear.title: Clear a search in one go
tips.searchTranscripts.text: The Sessions tab searches every session's name, date and transcript (Ctrl+F there): the tree keeps what matches, and a hit opens the conversation at that message.
tips.searchTranscripts.title: Search every past session
tips.sessionCleanup.text: The Sessions tab's Clean Up Old Sessions… button archives or deletes every session last active more than {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}, {week, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} or {month, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago. Running sessions and the one you're reading are left alone.
tips.sessionCleanup.title: Clear out old sessions
tips.sessionSizes.text: The Sessions tab shows each session's transcript size. One in amber is past Warn when a transcript is over: hand its work over to a new conversation to keep things quick.
tips.sessionSizes.title: Spot the conversations that grew too long
tips.sessionToolbar.text: The chip above the panes counts your agents by state; its ▾ lists them, most urgent first: choose one to go to it. Panes | Tiles beside it switches between the agents' terminals and a small tile each.
tips.sessionToolbar.title: Jump to any agent, or see them all as tiles
tips.sessionTree.text: In the Sessions tab, right-click a provider, an agent or a session with sub-sessions to archive or delete everything in it at once. Running sessions and ones in use are skipped, and Hive says which.
tips.sessionTree.title: Clear out a whole branch of sessions
tips.shareTemplates.text: The Templates view (activity bar) and a project's Templates tab list every template. Export… saves one as a file for teammates; Import… brings one in, for the workspace or a project.
tips.shareTemplates.title: Share agent templates
tips.sharedNotes.text: Shared notes and handovers live in the workspace, so every project's agents can read them with Hive's tools.
tips.sharedNotes.title: Notes every project shares
tips.signInExpired.text: If Claude Code's or Codex's sign-in expires, its agents show Needs sign-in (a violet dot) and you're told once. Sign in again, then Resume All Agents in the project header carries on the ones that stopped.
tips.signInExpired.title: When a sign-in expires
tips.silentUnknown.text: Hive never guesses an agent is idle: when its turn has been silent for a while with no sign of its end, its pane says so. If its terminal waits at its prompt, Mark idle puts it right.
tips.silentUnknown.title: An agent silent with its state unknown
tips.sortTables.text: Click a column's header in Hive's tables (shortcuts, Performance, Storage, the Overviews) to sort by it, again for the other way. Hive remembers each table's sort and rows per page.
tips.sortTables.title: Sort any table
tips.staleMessages.text: When the Assistant relays something about a card's current round, it ties the message to that card: if the card passes or starts another round before the agent reads it, Hive drops it as stale, so no agent reopens a passed card for an old finding.
tips.staleMessages.title: A message about a round goes stale, not late
tips.startNewAll.text: Start New in the project header's Agents menu gives every agent a new session after one question; Archive and Start New archives their old ones first. Their conversations stay in the Sessions tab.
tips.startNewAll.title: Fresh sessions for every agent
tips.storageCleanup.text: Project Settings → Storage shows how much space a project's backups, archive, attachments and worktrees take. Clean Up… moves old attachments and backups to the Recycle Bin, and shows you exactly what goes first.
tips.storageCleanup.title: See what Hive keeps, and clean up
tips.taskbarBadge.text: Hive's taskbar button shows how many agents need you, and flashes when one asks you something while Hive is in the background.
tips.taskbarBadge.title: Glance at the taskbar
tips.templateNames.text: Agent names are unique across the workspace. Loading a template from another project, give its agents new names in the list beside the template's own: Load template waits until none is taken.
tips.templateNames.title: Name a template's agents as you load it
tips.templateWorktrees.text: Loading a template puts an agent back in the clean worktree of its name, its branch left as it is, instead of making a new one. Old worktrees that are merged and clean can go too: tick the box in the Load dialog.
tips.templateWorktrees.title: Templates reuse worktrees
tips.testedClis.text: Claude Code, Codex and Copilot update on their own. Agent Setup shows the version this Hive release was tested with next to the one you have, and says when yours is newer or older.
tips.testedClis.title: See which CLI versions Hive was tested with
tips.tileStrip.text: In an agent's focus view (Tiles), the strip on the left shows each agent's card as a small chip, tinted with the colour of the board column it is in; click one to open the card. Drag the strip's edge to make it wider, and double-click the edge to reset it.
tips.tileStrip.title: Each agent's card, beside its name
tips.tilesView.text: Tiles shows each agent as a small tile: its state, status, card, progress and latest reply, twelve to a page. Click one to open its pane large beside the others; Esc goes back. Settings → Sessions → Tile order can put the agents waiting for you first.
tips.tilesView.title: See a whole team at once as tiles
tips.twoProviders.text: Agents in one project can use different providers: say a Codex reviewer next to a Claude Code agent. Hand Over to… passes work between them.
tips.twoProviders.title: Mix Claude Code and Codex
tips.ui.counter: {total, plural, one {Tip · {n, number} of #} other {Tip · {n, number} of #}}
tips.ui.showOnStart: Show a tip when Hive starts
tips.ui.title: Tips
tips.unexpectedClose.text: If Hive was ended without quitting (a crash, or something closed it), the next start says when it was last seen and which agents were running, with Resume All. Settings → Sessions → Resume agents after an unexpected close resumes them by itself.
tips.unexpectedClose.title: Know when Hive closed unexpectedly
tips.unmerged.text: The agent's tab shows how many commits aren't merged yet, Merge… in its ⋯ menu says what is left, and Git → Changes shows everything the agent changed since it branched.
tips.unmerged.title: See what a worktree agent has to merge
tips.unusedWorktrees.text: Removed an agent but kept its worktree? Git → Changes opens on the worktrees no agent uses, saying who made each: open one to see its work and merge it, remove the merged ones with their branches, or give one back to an agent.
tips.unusedWorktrees.title: Tidy kept worktrees
tips.viewerTokens.text: An app that shows what your agents are doing, such as Apiary, needs only a viewer token: Settings → Agent API → Viewer tokens makes one that can read everything and change nothing, and revokes it again.
tips.viewerTokens.title: Let another app watch Hive
tips.workspaceMoved.text: Moved the workspace folder, say to another drive? Open it from its new place and choose Repair… in the banner: agents' worktrees, their sessions, and Claude Code's conversations and memory follow it.
tips.workspaceMoved.title: Move a workspace without losing its agents
tips.worktreeReuse.text: Adding an agent with a new worktree named like one you kept (B4, and B4's worktree is unused)? If it's merged and clean, Hive gives the agent that folder, brought up to main: its node_modules are already there.
tips.worktreeReuse.title: A kept worktree is used again
tips.worktrees.text: In Add Agent…, choose New worktree: the agent works on its own branch, and Merge… brings its work back when you're happy with it.
tips.worktrees.title: Give an agent its own worktree
